   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  CITY CLERK’S OFFICE

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons

 FROM:  Huma Ahmed, City Clerk

 DATE:  August 14, 2024

 SUBJECT:  Commission Applicant Residency Requirements and Spouses Serving
  on Commissions

 ATTACHMENTS:  1. BHMC 2-2-104 (B) – Commissioner Residency
  2. City Commissioners’ Handbook (Page 29)
  3. City Council Policy and Operations Manual (Page 33)

INTRODUCTION

In a recent review of the City Council Policy and Operations Manual, the City Commissioners’
Handbook and the Beverly Hills Municipal Code (BHMC), staff is seeking guidance regarding
applicant residency requirements along with spousal participation on City Commissions.

The Beverly Hills Municipal Code is the legal guiding document for City rules and regulations.
Both the City Council Policy and Operations Manual and Commissioners’ Handbook are
documents that reflect City Council direction on policy matters and are considered ‘established
practices.’ There is a discrepancy between the BHMC and the two afore mentioned handbooks.

Staff is seeking clarification and further direction from the City Council Liaisons (Vice Mayor
Sharona R. Nazarian, PsyD and Councilmember Craig A. Corman) regarding the applicability of
these provisions.

DISCUSSION

Commission Applicant Residency

Commissioners are appointed by the City Council for an initial two-year term and may be
reappointed for an additional four years at the discretion of the City Council (unless directed
otherwise).

It has been an established practice of the City to solicit applications from residents with a minimum
two-year residency in Beverly Hills. The City Council Handbook lists this requirement, but both
the BHMC and the Commissioners’ Handbook do not. Research into the matter indicates that the
two-year residency policy appears to have first been established in 1967 and then again
reaffirmed in 2001 by the then City Council. However, BHMC (2-2-105) was not updated to reflect
the adoption of this policy, but rather, it became an established practice of the City.
 Additionally, neither the policy nor the established practice indicates if an applicant must be a
resident for consecutive years immediately preceding their application submittal, or if intermittent
residency is permitted to count towards the two-year requirement. Staff is seeking further
guidance on this matter.

Spouses Serving on Commissions

Separately, the City Commissioners’ Handbook lists that spouses cannot serve concurrently or
consecutively on the ‘same’ commission. The handbook states the City Council has discretion
about placing spouses on different commissions, although it is discouraged. The BHMC has not
been updated to reflect any direction related to spouses on commissions.

FISCAL IMPACT

None.
RECOMMENDATION

Staff respectfully requests the City Council Liaisons review and provide feedback on:

  1. Shall the BHMC be updated to reflect the City’s established practice of a two-year
  residency requirement for commissioner applications?
  2. If a two-year residency is recommended, shall it be for consecutive years immediately
  preceding an application submittal or intermittent years?
  3. Is there an interest to further update the direction regarding spouses serving on different
  commissions at the same time?
  4. Shall the BHMC be updated to reflect new direction or established direction already
  provided in Commissioners’ Handbook, pending City Council approval?

Should there be direction to update the BHMC, then staff will present the City Council Liaisons’
recommendations to the City Council at a future meeting. The request will also include a formal
update to the Beverly Hills Municipal Code so that all three documents (BHMC, City Council Policy
and Operations Manual and the Commissioners’ Handbook) are standardized and consistent.

   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  POLICE DEPARTMENT

  MEMORANDUM

  TO:  Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons

  FROM:  Mark G. Stainbrook, Chief of Police

  DATE:  August 14, 2024

  SUBJECT:  Review of Charitable Solicitation Commission Duties

INTRODUCTION
At the most recent meeting of the Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons
on May 14, 2024, the Liaisons requested that staff begin looking at the history and duties
of various commissions to determine whether a given commission’s duties are still relevant
or could be merged with another commission. In particular, the Liaisons requested that
staff return with information regarding the duties of the Charitable Solicitations Commission.
The City first began regulating charitable solicitations in 1942 (Ordinance No. 562) in
response to numerous individuals conducting unscrupulous solicitation of funds and other
assets, largely related to supporting the war effort, when in reality the funds were being
used for their own personal gain. The 1942 ordinance created a framework of regulations
intended to prevent fraudulent solicitations, and in 1962 a “Solicitations Advisory
Commission”, which is now the Charitable Solicitations Commission (CSC), was created
(Ordinance No. 1145).
Presently, the primary responsibility of the CSC is to ensure the compliance of charitable
organizations that solicit donations or funds from Beverly Hills residents. The goal of the
Commission is to protect our community from fraudulent, fictitious, or otherwise
unscrupulous solicitations and keep the community aware of the many charitable events
held in Beverly Hills. In coordination with the Police Department, the Commission regulates
solicitation permit issuance, reviews charities' financial statements, and maintains a
dedicated website for the public to obtain information regarding permitted solicitations.
There is no cost to apply for a permit.
Beverly Hills Municipal Code Section 4-3-80 indicates that after filing the application, the
application shall be submitted to the CSC for review and recommendation. The Commission
shall review the application and shall also review any information furnished by the Police
Department based on their investigation of the applicant, and the Commission shall then
make a recommendation to the City of Beverly Hills official empowered by the City to grant
 or deny the permit. (Ordinance No. 17-O-2738). The Commission meets monthly to review
permits.

BACKGROUND
Upon examining the regulatory framework of neighboring cities of Santa Monica, West
Hollywood, and Culver City, these jurisdictions do not require a specific permit for charitable
solicitations, and instead rely on broader state or county-level regulation to govern such
activities. Notably, these broader state and county-level regulations largely did not exist at
the time that Beverly Hills first adopted its regulations.

  City of Los Angeles
  The City of Los Angeles does require nonprofit organizations to obtain a charitable
  solicitation permit and provide a financial statement. Still, its process does not mirror
  that of the City of Beverly Hills. The City of Los Angeles Charitable Services Section
  is responsible for regulating and monitoring Charitable activities, Bingo Gaming
  Enforcement, and investigations related to non-profit organizations throughout the
  City of Los Angeles. The Section is comprised of civilian investigators and
  administrative personnel whose main function is to ensure charitable and non-profit
  organizations comply with Section 44.04, Article 4, of the Los Angeles Municipal
  Code and the City’s Charitable Solicitation Ordinance No. 185,605. All activity
  regulated by the Charitable Services Section is examined, and analysis reports are
  acted upon by the Police Permit Review Panel, which is empowered by the Board of
  Police Commissioners.

  County of Los Angeles
  The County of Los Angeles mandates a permit for charitable solicitations, covering
  a broad spectrum of organizations and activities. The Business License Commission
  holds hearings for business licenses within the unincorporated areas of Los Angeles
  County. It also reviews full non-profit organizations wishing to solicit within the
  unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County; however, this does not include the City
  of Beverly Hills.

  Public Access to Nonprofit Information
  Since nonprofit organizations must file Form 990 with the IRS annually, anybody can
  review a nonprofit’s finances utilizing online resources. Additionally, program
  spending information can be found in Part III of Form 990; some nonprofits include
  program descriptions in supplemental information at the end of the document.
 ANALYSIS
  CSC-Provided Information: The information provided by the CSC enables Beverly
  Hills residents to thoroughly evaluate the efficiency of events and fundraising
  campaigns targeting funds from residents. However, this information is also able to
  be provided directly by the Beverly Hills Police Department (BHPD) staff that process
  the permits.
  Regulatory Alignment: Aligning our regulatory approach with the regulations of
  neighboring cities West Hollywood, Santa Monica, Culver City, and the City of Los
  Angeles would simplify the process for charitable organizations and may encourage
  greater compliance and participation in charitable activities.
  The City of Los Angeles does require a permit and reviews financial statements.
  However, they do not support a Commission. Permit issuance and financial
  statement reviews are performed by Los Angeles Police Department administrative
  personnel. They charge a $42 application fee and ensure that the applicants are in
  compliance with the Department of Justice (DOJ).
  Resource Allocation: The resources devoted to maintaining the City of Beverly Hills
  Charitable Solicitations Commission and monthly meetings could be redirected
  towards more impactful initiatives, particularly those that directly support and
  enhance charitable activities and public welfare.

RECOMMENDATION
Based on the analysis and considerations outlined above, staff seeks direction from the
Liaisons regarding the duties of the CSC and whether those duties should be modified or
transferred to BHPD staff. Any recommendations developed by the Liaisons will be
presented to the full City Council at a future date for consideration.

CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Commission Standardization Ad Hoc
  Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Wednesday, August 14, 2024
  2:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  August 14, 2024 / 2:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember Craig Corman, Assistant
  City Manager Ryan Gohlich, City Clerk Huma Ahmed, Municipal Affairs
  Manager Cynthia Owens, Police Captain Max Subin

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Kimberly Vinokur, Chair of the Cultural Heritage Commission: She wishes for the
  committee to look into two items. First is how the City deals with commissioners
  who miss meetings, as the current procedure does not really work for her
  commission as they only meet four times a year. She also wishes for the prohibition
  of the use of cell phones by commissioners during meetings laid out in the
  commissioner’s handbook to have its enforcement mechanism strengthened.

  2) Commission Applicant Residency Requirements and Spouses Serving on
  Commissions:
  a. Presentation by Huma Ahmed:
  i. The City has three guiding documents that cover the standards that
  commissioners must follow, the City Council Policy and Operations
  Manual, the City Commissioners’ Handbook, and the Beverly Hills
  Municipal Code.
  ii. Staff have expressed an interest in creating consistency between the three
  documents.
  iii. The city currently has a two-year minimum residency requirement for
  commission applicants, which was first established in 1967 and reaffirmed
  in 2001. However, this practice is not part of the Municipal Code.
  iv. The residency requirement also does not clarify whether the two-year
  residency requirement must be two consecutive years prior to applying or
  if a prospective commissioner can live in the city for two years, move away,
  and then return to the city later and immediately apply.
  v. Staff is requesting direction on if the Municipal Code should be updated to
  reflect the two-year residency requirement and if so should it be for the
  consecutive years immediately preceding an application or can they be
  intermittent.
  b. The municipal code currently requires all commissioners must be residents of the
  city while they serve, with the exceptions of the Architectural Design and Review
 Highlights for August 14, 2024
Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee

  Commission if they are unable to find a licensed architect or landscape architect
  within the city and for commissioners who move out of the city for a temporary
  basis such as during a remodel of a home or during a divorce.
  c. Councilmember Corman is in favor of commissioner requirements being in the
  Municipal Code rather than just a policy document, but he would like the city to first
  make sure what it wants in the policy manual before it edits the municipal code to
  reflect the manual.
  d. Councilmember Corman is also in favor of having the two year residency
  requirement be continuous and ongoing when a commissioner is appointed.
  e. Vice Mayor Nazarian also desires for the City’s three guiding documents to be
  consistent. She also wishes for any additional items that come up in the future
  dealing with the consistency between the three documents to be brought to the Ad
  Hoc.
  f. She agrees with Councilmember Corman’s stance on the residency requirement.
  g. Presentation by Huma Ahmed:
  i. The Commissioner’s handbook currently states that spouses cannot serve
  on the same commission at the same time, but that they can serve on
  different commissions with the approval of Council, but this is strongly
  discouraged.
  ii. The Municipal Code does not include any restrictions on spouses serving
  on the same or separate commissions.
  h. Councilmember Corman believes that whatever decision is reached about this
  issue, it should be reflected in the Municipal Code.
  i. The councilmember also agreed with the current policy barring spouses from
  serving on the same commission and believes that it should be extended to barring
  spouses, children, parents, or people living in the same household from serving on
  the same commission.
  j. He also believes that there should be a one-year gap between a commissioner
  leaving the commission and their spouse being able to apply.
  k. He is also uncomfortable with the language around “discouraging” spouses from
  serving on different commissions but differed his decision on the matter to the Vice
  Mayor.
  l. The Vice Mayor is opposed to having spouses serve on different commissions as
  she feels that it detracts from the idea that commissioners should bring their
  different and unique perspectives on issues to the City.
  m. The Vice Mayor would also like there to be a cap on how many commissions a
  person can serve on.
  n. Councilmember Corman believes that the cap on the number of commissions a
  person can serve on should be three.
  o. He is also open to discussing potential restrictions on in-laws on the same
  commission.
  p. Neither Liaison wishes for an exception for spouses to serve concurrently if one
  spouse is on the planning commission.
  q. Public Comment, Kimberly Vinokur: She lives with one of her fellow commissioners
  and spoke about the difficulties this presented in order to prevent Brown Act
  violations. When it comes to term limits, she is in favor of a three-term limit in order
  to prevent the appearance of favoritism. She would also like the number of
  meetings a commissioner missed prior to reprimands being issued to be lowered
 Highlights for August 14, 2024
Commission Standardization Ad Hoc Committee

  for commissions that only meet four times a year such as the Cultural Heritage
  Commission.
  r.  There have been some statements from City Staff about how they would like to
  refine how a resident is legally defined, whether that be that someone must be a
  registered voter in the city, must physically live in the city, or that they must own
  property in the city.

  3) Review of Charitable Solicitation Commission Duties:
  a. The Commission accepts applications for events at a hotel, fundraisers, or other
  charitable events.
  b. Police Captain Max Subin pulls and signs submitted applications should they meet
  certain guidelines, after which it is sent to the commission for review.
  c. Following an approved event taking place, a financial statement must be submitted
  within 60 days.
  d. The Commission pushes for at least 50% of all proceeds from the charitable event
  to be donated, but this is not in the code.
  e. The Commission has never denied an application since Captain Subin started
  working with the commission.
  f. The Commission relies mostly on information submitted in the application as well
  as the publicly available fundraising financial document.
  g. The Charitable Solicitations regulations were adopted in 1942, before the creation
  of most state and federal laws regulating charities.
  h. The Commission was founded in 1962.
  i. The Commission would like to see a requirement that at least 50% of net revenue
  of a charity event be donated.
  j. The 1942 regulations were adopted to deal with scammers who would pretend to
  be aiding the war effort when in reality they were pocketing the donations.
  k. Nowadays, applicants can be easily examined with websites that display
  everything about a 501(c)(3).
  l. The only work that would be cut out by staff if the Commission was replaced by
  staff is that staff would no longer need to prepare agendas and agenda packets.
  m. Councilmember Corman would like to investigate potentially vetting charities for
  how they use donated funds.
  n. Both Liaisons are in favor of sunsetting the Commission as they feel that the
  Commission has devolved into an administrative proceeding.
  o. The Liaisons recommend sunsetting the Commission either in June 2025, when
  the number of Commissioners will drop to three, or in December of 2025, when
  there will only be two commissioners left.
  p. Councilmember Corman would like for at least 50% of Charity proceeds to be
  spent on charity work rather than overhead.

  4) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: August 14, 2024 / 3:24 PM
